column1: “What has he done for my state?”
column2: Can I ask which state you're in? Across the country there are two big changes: states and councils now receive far more money every month, and federal roads and projects are under way in every zone. Let me tell you what's happening near you.
column3: FAAC H1 2026: states shared ₦4.47tn, councils ₦3.13tn. Then use the zone card (South-East, North, South-South).

column2: You deserve better from your council. In 2024 the Supreme Court, in a case brought by the Federal Government, ruled that councils must receive their allocations directly, not through the governor. The money is going to councils, so ask your chairman what he's done with it.
column3: Supreme Court ruling, July 2024, covering all 774 LGAs. Councils received ₦3.13tn in H1 2026.

column2: As Works Minister Umahi points out, the South-East now holds the Works ministry for the first time, and over ₦1.3 trillion is committed to its roads and bridges, including the Enugu-Onitsha road and the Second Niger Bridge access roads. The South-East Development Commission was also created by law in 2024.
column3: Figures from Works Minister Umahi. Don't claim the bridge itself (finished before Tinubu) or that SEDC is fully funded.

column2: Major northern projects are under way: the Abuja-Kaduna-Kano road (the Kano section is reported about 95% done), Sokoto-Gusau-Funtua-Zaria, the AKK gas pipeline and Kaduna-Kano rail. The North also has more appointment slots than the South.
column3: Mostly government figures; the appointment list was withdrawn over errors, so don't quote exact counts.

column2: Every zone has appointees, and federal character isn't just about ethnicity. The NNPC chief, for example, is Yoruba but from Kwara in the North-Central. If a voter has a specific concern about their zone, note it and we'll follow up.
column3: Don't quote zone counts as final; the Presidency withdrew its list over errors.
